A few miles from Boston, in Massachusetts, a narrow inlet winds far into the country and ends in a thickly wooded swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> According to an old story, Kidd the pirate buried a great treasure under one of the giant oaks that stand beside this inlet. <break time="0.8s" /> Kidd never returned for it, because soon afterward he was arrested in Boston, sent to England, and executed as a pirate. <break time="0.8s" /> People also say that the devil himself watched over the hiding of the gold and has guarded it closely ever since. <break time="0.8s" /> About the year 1727, there lived near this place a mean, greedy man named Tom Walker, who had a wife as miserly as himself. <break time="0.8s" /> So miserly were the two that they even tried to cheat each other, and whatever the wife could get her hands on, she hid away. <break time="0.8s" /> They quarreled so loudly and so often that a lonely traveler passing their house would stop to listen and then hurry on his way. <break time="0.8s" /> Their house stood alone in a bare field, and like its owners, it had a hungry, half starved look about it. <break time="0.8s" /> A miserable horse, its ribs showing like the bars of a grill, wandered about the field in search of something to eat.

보스턴에서 몇 마일 떨어진 곳. <break time="0.8s" /> 매사추세츠주에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 좁은 후미가 내륙 깊숙이 굽이쳐 들어간다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 나무가 빽빽한 늪에서 끝난다. <break time="0.8s" /> 옛이야기에 따르면. <break time="0.8s" /> 해적 키드가 엄청난 보물을 묻었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 거대한 참나무 중 한 그루 아래에. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 후미 옆에 서 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 키드는 그것을 찾으러 끝내 돌아오지 못했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 얼마 뒤 그가 보스턴에서 체포되어. <break time="0.8s" /> 영국으로 보내져. <break time="0.8s" /> 해적으로 처형되었기 때문이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들은 또 말한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 악마가 직접 지켜보았다고 금을 숨기는 일을. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그 뒤로 줄곧 그것을 단단히 지켜 왔다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 1727년 무렵. <break time="0.8s" /> 이곳 근처에 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 톰 워커라는 인색하고 욕심 많은 남자가. <break time="0.8s" /> 그에게는 자기만큼이나 인색한 아내가 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 두 사람은 너무나 인색했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 서로를 속이려고까지 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 아내는 손에 넣을 수 있는 것이면 무엇이든 감춰 두었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들은 너무 시끄럽게 자주 다투었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그 집 앞을 지나가던 외로운 나그네는. <break time="0.8s" /> 멈춰 서서 귀를 기울이곤 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러고는 서둘러 제 갈 길을 갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들의 집은 헐벗은 들판에 홀로 서 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 주인들처럼. <break time="0.8s" /> 굶주려 반쯤 말라 버린 듯한 모습이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 비참한 몰골의 말 한 마리가. <break time="0.8s" /> 갈비뼈가 석쇠 살처럼 드러난 채. <break time="0.8s" /> 들판을 헤매고 다녔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 먹을 것을 찾아.

One day Tom took a shortcut through the swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> A gloomy place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where tall pines and hemlocks. <break time="0.8s" /> Made it dark even at noon. <break time="0.8s" /> Moving as carefully as a cat. <break time="0.8s" /> He picked his way along fallen tree trunks. <break time="0.8s" /> For green moss hid. <break time="0.8s" /> Deep pools of black mud. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he reached a firm piece of ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Where Native Americans had once built a fort. <break time="0.8s" /> During their wars with the first settlers. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting down on a fallen tree to rest. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom poked at the soil with his stick. <break time="0.8s" /> And turned up an old skull. <break time="0.8s" /> From those wars. <break time="0.8s" /> Lifting his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom saw a huge stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting on a stump right in front of him. <break time="0.8s" /> Though he had not heard anyone approach. <break time="0.8s" /> The mans face was dark and dirty with soot. <break time="0.8s" /> As if he worked among fires. <break time="0.8s" /> And a heavy axe rested on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> What are you doing on my grounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Growled the stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> But Tom answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That the land belonged to Deacon Peabody. <break time="0.8s" /> The stranger pointed to a tall tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Which looked healthy on the outside. <break time="0.8s" /> But was rotten at the core. <break time="0.8s" /> With Peabodys name carved on its bark. <break time="0.8s" /> Nearby lay another great tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Already cut down. <break time="0.8s" /> Which bore the name of Crowninshield. <break time="0.8s" /> A rich man. <break time="0.8s" /> Said to have made his fortune as a pirate.

One day Tom took a shortcut through the swamp, a gloomy place where tall pines and hemlocks made it dark even at noon. <break time="0.8s" /> Moving as carefully as a cat, he picked his way along fallen tree trunks, for green moss hid deep pools of black mud. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he reached a firm piece of ground, where Native Americans had once built a fort during their wars with the first settlers. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting down on a fallen tree to rest, Tom poked at the soil with his stick and turned up an old skull from those wars. <break time="0.8s" /> Lifting his eyes, Tom saw a huge stranger sitting on a stump right in front of him, though he had not heard anyone approach. <break time="0.8s" /> The mans face was dark and dirty with soot, as if he worked among fires, and a heavy axe rested on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> What are you doing on my grounds, growled the stranger, but Tom answered that the land belonged to Deacon Peabody. <break time="0.8s" /> The stranger pointed to a tall tree, which looked healthy on the outside but was rotten at the core, with Peabodys name carved on its bark. <break time="0.8s" /> Nearby lay another great tree, already cut down, which bore the name of Crowninshield, a rich man said to have made his fortune as a pirate.

어느 날 톰은 늪을 가로지르는 지름길로 갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳은 음침한 곳이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서는 키 큰 소나무와 솔송나무들이. <break time="0.8s" /> 한낮에도 주위를 어둡게 만들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 고양이처럼 조심스럽게 움직이며. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 쓰러진 나무줄기를 따라 한 걸음씩 골라 디뎠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 초록 이끼가 감추고 있었기 때문이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 시커먼 진흙의 깊은 웅덩이를. <break time="0.8s" /> 마침내 그는 단단한 땅에 이르렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에는 예전에 아메리카 원주민들이 요새를 지었었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 초기 정착민들과 전쟁을 벌이던 시절에. <break time="0.8s" /> 쉬려고 쓰러진 나무 위에 앉아. <break time="0.8s" /> 톰은 지팡이로 흙을 쿡쿡 찔렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 오래된 해골 하나를 파냈다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 전쟁 때의. <break time="0.8s" /> 눈을 들어. <break time="0.8s" /> 톰은 덩치 큰 낯선 사내를 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 사내는 바로 앞 그루터기에 앉아 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 누가 다가오는 소리를 듣지 못했는데도. <break time="0.8s" /> 사내의 얼굴은 그을음으로 시커멓고 더러웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 마치 불 속에서 일하는 사람처럼. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 무거운 도끼가 그의 어깨에 얹혀 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 내 땅에서 뭘 하고 있나. <break time="0.8s" /> 낯선 사내가 으르렁거리듯 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 톰은 대답했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 땅은 피바디 집사의 것이라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 사내는 키 큰 나무 한 그루를 가리켰다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 나무는 겉으로는 튼튼해 보였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 속은 썩어 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 껍질에는 피바디의 이름이 새겨져 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 근처에는 또 다른 큰 나무가 누워 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이미 베어진 채. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 나무에는 크라운인실드라는 이름이 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 부자였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 해적질로 재산을 모았다고들 했다.

When Tom asked who he was the stranger said that he went by many names. <break time="0.8s" /> And Tom realized. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was talking to Old Scratch. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Meeting such a figure. <break time="0.8s" /> Would have frightened most men. <break time="0.8s" /> But Tom had lived so long with a fierce wife. <break time="0.8s" /> That he did not fear even the devil. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Scratch offered him Kidds treasure. <break time="0.8s" /> On certain conditions. <break time="0.8s" /> Which must have been hard. <break time="0.8s" /> Since Tom asked for time to think them over. <break time="0.8s" /> As proof the devil pressed a finger on Toms forehead. <break time="0.8s" /> And when Tom got home. <break time="0.8s" /> He found a black fingerprint. <break time="0.8s" /> Burned into his skin. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom told his wife the whole secret. <break time="0.8s" /> And she, greedy for the hidden gold. <break time="0.8s" /> Urged him to accept the bargain at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of pure stubbornness Tom refused. <break time="0.8s" /> So she decided to make the deal herself. <break time="0.8s" /> And keep all the gold for herself. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening she set off for the swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> With the silver teapot and spoons. <break time="0.8s" /> Tied up in her apron. <break time="0.8s" /> And she never came back. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for her at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom found her apron hanging in a tree. <break time="0.8s" /> And the ground below was trampled. <break time="0.8s" /> As if by a fierce struggle. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing clumps of black hair there. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom guessed that she had fought the devil hard. <break time="0.8s" /> And the loss of his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Made up for the loss of his silver.

When Tom asked who he was, the stranger said that he went by many names, and Tom realized that he was talking to Old Scratch, the devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Meeting such a figure would have frightened most men, but Tom had lived so long with a fierce wife that he did not fear even the devil. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Scratch offered him Kidds treasure on certain conditions, which must have been hard, since Tom asked for time to think them over. <break time="0.8s" /> As proof, the devil pressed a finger on Toms forehead, and when Tom got home, he found a black fingerprint burned into his skin. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom told his wife the whole secret, and she, greedy for the hidden gold, urged him to accept the bargain at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of pure stubbornness Tom refused, so she decided to make the deal herself and keep all the gold for herself. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening she set off for the swamp with the silver teapot and spoons tied up in her apron, and she never came back. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for her at last, Tom found her apron hanging in a tree, and the ground below was trampled as if by a fierce struggle. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing clumps of black hair there, Tom guessed that she had fought the devil hard, and the loss of his wife made up for the loss of his silver.

톰이 그가 누구냐고 묻자 사내는 자기가 여러 이름으로 불린다고 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러자 톰은 깨달았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기가 올드 스크래치와 이야기하고 있다는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 바로 악마 그 자신과. <break time="0.8s" /> 그런 존재를 만났다면. <break time="0.8s" /> 대부분의 사람은 겁에 질렸을 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 톰은 사나운 아내와 너무 오래 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 악마조차 두려워하지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 올드 스크래치는 그에게 키드의 보물을 주겠다고 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 몇 가지 조건을 걸고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 조건은 틀림없이 까다로웠을 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 톰이 생각할 시간을 달라고 했으니까. <break time="0.8s" /> 증거로 악마는 톰의 이마에 손가락을 눌렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 톰이 집에 돌아와 보니. <break time="0.8s" /> 검은 지문 하나가 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 살갗에 타 들어간 채로. <break time="0.8s" /> 톰은 아내에게 비밀을 모두 털어놓았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러자 숨겨진 금에 욕심이 난 아내는. <break time="0.8s" /> 당장 거래를 받아들이라고 그를 재촉했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 순전히 고집 때문에 톰은 거절했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 아내는 직접 거래를 하기로 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 금을 모두 혼자 차지하기로. <break time="0.8s" /> 어느 날 저녁 아내는 늪으로 떠났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 은 찻주전자와 숟가락들을. <break time="0.8s" /> 앞치마에 싸 든 채. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 다시는 돌아오지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 마침내 아내를 찾아 나선 톰은. <break time="0.8s" /> 나무에 걸린 아내의 앞치마를 발견했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그 아래 땅은 짓밟혀 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 격렬한 몸싸움이라도 벌어진 것처럼. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서 검은 머리카락 뭉치를 보고. <break time="0.8s" /> 톰은 아내가 악마와 거세게 싸웠으리라 짐작했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 아내를 잃은 것이. <break time="0.8s" /> 은그릇을 잃은 것을 달래 주었다.
